discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background with WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model and the properties of primordial perturbations
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, conceived and led by Bennett, with Page directing the instrument and Spergel the theoretical analysis, turned cosmology into a precision science. Its full-sky temperature and polarization maps showed that the universe is spatially flat and fixed its age, composition and baryon and dark-matter densities to percent-level precision. WMAP found that primordial perturbations are adiabatic, nearly Gaussian and slightly tilted away from scale invariance. These are the signatures predicted by inflation, so the measurements gave quantitative support to physics of the first instants. Its polarization data measured the optical depth to reionization and detected the temperature-polarization correlations predicted by theory. The team's careful, conservative treatment of systematics and foregrounds set the standard for Planck and for today's searches for inflationary B-modes. The six-parameter Lambda-CDM model that WMAP established is now the foundation of modern cosmology.
